To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
fluctuations in the fluxes of supernovae induced by large-scale peculiar velocity offer a promising method for measuring large-scale peculiar velocity at intermediate redshift.
type Ia supernova flux variations induced by LSP velocity are a promising probe for LSPV at z similar to 1.
type Ia supernova observations can be used to measure the large-scale peculiar velocity field at intermediate redshift (z similar to 0-1) by using the flux fluctuations induced by LSPVs.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the measurement of the large scale peculiar velocity of the dark matter, dark matter, and dark energy at cosmological scales
the measurement of LSPV with type Ia supernova flux fluctuations, which will be a new window for probing dark matter, dark matter, and gravity.
the application of the supernova flux fluctuations to LSPV measurements, and the corresponding theoretical analysis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
type Ia supernova flux fluctuations are a promising probe of LSPV at redshifts z similar to 1, and the systematical error can be well suppressed.

type Ia supernova fluxes are a promising probe to measure LSPVs at intermediate redshift, and the measurement can be further improved with future supernova observations. (C) 2022 by the American Astronomical Society.
the LSPV measurement through the supernova flux fluctuations is a powerful and promising method to probe dark matter and dark energy.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the LSPV can be detected at 3 sigma level in the 3D space with a sample of 10(4) type Ia supernova light curves, and a 1 sigma uncertainty in the LSPV measurement can be achieved with a sample of similar to 10(5) type Ia light curves.
type Ia supernova fluxes, which are the most abundant cosmological standard candles in the Universe, are a promising probe to measure LSPVs, and thus the dark universe.

, with a supernova survey of 10,000 supernovae, we can measure LSPV to 1% precision, which is competitive with the current best measurement of LSPV from the Cosmicflows-3 project, and the upcoming LSPV measurements from the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument and the Large Synoptic Survey Telescope.
The main takeaway from our work is that
type Ia supernova observations are a promising tool to probe LSPV, which can be used to constrain the growth rate of structure, the nature of dark matter, and the properties of dark energy.
LSPV can be measured with high accuracy and low systematical error using type Ia supernova fluxes.
type Ia supernova fluxes can serve as a new probe of LSPV, which will be complementary to galaxy peculiar velocities.
